newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks low, opportunities seen.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks low, opportunities seen.

text.p: Directionless trading and lack of interest among investors drove prices down on the Cypriot stock market during the week, traders and analysts said.
The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) general index closed at 81.12, losing 1.09 points from last week's close of 82.21.
On Friday the market appeared to show signs of a recovery, gaining from its opening level of 80.57 with many stocks recouping on losses made in the week.
Weekly volume settled at 2.92 million pounds ($6.3 million) compared to 2.95 million pounds during the previous week between November 18 and 22.
"The market is lacking direction," one floor trader said.
The Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation (CISCO) said in a weekly report the downtrend is soon expected to reverse with low prices bound to attract investors.
"Institutional as well as individual investors are expected to re-evaluate their investment policies in the light of the recent retreat of the market and engage in selective buying," it said.

Banking shares slid two percent, to 89.21 from 91.04. Fully paid shares in the Bank of Cyprus closed at 333.5, down six cents from last week. Fully paid shares of the Cyprus Popular Bank shed 8.5 cents to close at 321.5.
The Hellenic Bank closed at 260.5, down 6.5 cents in the week. Shares in the Universal Savings Bank rose four cents to close at 139.
Insurance stocks closed the week 2.04 percent weaker, with its sub index falling to 57.57 from 59.08.
Universal Life shares dropped four cents to close at 378. Paneuropean Insurance fully paid lost 3.5 cents to close at 125.5.
Interamerican Insurance fully paid closed at 99.5, down two cents. Philiki Insurance fully paid declined 10.5 cents, closing at 232.5.
Vassiliko, the cement producer, closed at 160.5, up six cents in the week. Beer and wine producers Keo, gained a cent to close at 109.
National carrier Cyprus Airways closed the week at 39.3 cents from 39.9 last week. On Tuesday it fell to a year low of 39 cents.
The Cyprus Trading Corporation closed at 123, down four cents. Woolworth Cyprus lost 1 cent, closing at 92.5. Zako clothes and accessories chain closed at 91.5 from 90 last week. ($=0.46 pounds)
